html:
In 1948, during the war that founded Israel, hundreds of thousands of Palestinians fled or were driven to the West Bank and across the Jordan river. Jordan took the West Bank in 1950 and gave Palestinians citizenship, the only Arab state to do so widely.

A second wave came in the Six-Day War of 1967, when Israel took the West Bank. Refugee camps around Amman and Zarqa grew into city districts. Palestinians became a large part, likely the majority, of Jordan's people, and led much of its business.

The arrival of armed Palestinian groups led to Black September in 1970. Questions of identity, between East Bankers and Palestinians, run through Jordan's politics. See also the Nakba.
